source_snapshot.procedure: Enable SNMPv3, load the MIB, expand `$target`, and use Get Next or Get Subtree.
source_snapshot.criteria: Use Net-SNMP get-type commands to retrieve `$target` values.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; substitutes a TLS-bypassed Redfish DateTime GET and calls the case monitor/configure.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED on read-versus-write interpretation and missing OID/encoding/tolerance/recovery.

old_problem: The old review interpreted the MIB path label `configureSP` as a possible imperative to write the clock despite every source action and criterion being a Get operation, then made that hypothetical SET fork the blocker.
disposition_reason: The executable source is unambiguous: load the project MIB and retrieve the `$target` subtree with Get Next/Get Subtree/get-type commands. The item string identifies the requested MIB path; no SET, test value, write criterion or restore step exists. This review therefore preserves a read-only SNMPv3 visibility/representation test and explicitly leaves clock-configuration coverage unclaimed.
decision_basis: XLSX row 761, same-row DeepSeek, the exact GPT V2 record and historical record were directly inspected.
RFC 3416 defines Get/GetNext as retrieval operations and SetRequest as the distinct write operation; the Master names only retrieval.
The exact numeric OIDs, ASN.1 syntax and access metadata must come from the platform-matched vendor MIB rather than a guessed public OID.
DMTF Redfish Manager DateTime is a different interface; it may be separate corroboration only and cannot replace the SNMP transport/MIB proof.

test_case.test_name: Retrieve and validate the project-defined `configureSP.spClock` subtree through SNMPv3
test_case.purpose: Verify the BMC exposes the exact platform MIB target represented by `configureSP.spClock` to an approved SNMPv3 user, returns all required child objects with valid types/encodings, and reports a clock representation consistent with the Project SPEC without changing BMC time.
required_package: Vendor MIB package matched to BMC model/firmware with hash and numeric expansion of `$target`
Project expected child-OID set, ASN.1 types, access metadata, clock format/timezone semantics and allowed read delta
Approved SNMPv3 engine/user/security level/auth/privacy profile with protected secret handling
Trusted synchronized reference clock; optional CA-validated Redfish Manager URI only if Project SPEC approves it as a separate cross-check
test_case.test_command: Operator enables the approved SNMPv3 profile in the actual WebUI and confirms redacted settings. On the management host, load the hashed vendor MIB, resolve `$target` to numeric OIDs, record MIB syntax/access, then execute authenticated SNMPv3 GETNEXT/GETBULK traversal limited to that subtree using credentials from a protected configuration store. Compare returned OID set/types/values and the decoded clock/timezone representation with the Project SPEC and a closely timestamped reference. Issue no SET. Redfish, if approved, is collected separately with normal CA validation.
test_case.expected_result: The symbolic target resolves using the approved MIB; every required child OID is returned exactly once through SNMPv3 with the documented syntax/access and decodes without error; the clock/timezone value is within the approved read-only tolerance of the synchronized reference; no out-of-subtree data, SNMP error, authentication downgrade or BMC time/log change occurs.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires the exact project MIB/hash, numeric target expansion, complete required child set, correct ASN.1 decoding, approved SNMPv3 security and clock comparison within a project-supplied tolerance. FAIL includes missing/extra required objects, type/encoding mismatch, stale/out-of-tolerance clock, auth/privacy failure or any mutation. Without the MIB or tolerance execution is NOT READY, not PASS. This result never claims SNMP SET/configuration coverage.
safety_gate: Allow only Get/GetNext/GetBulk; prohibit SNMP SET and Redfish PATCH
Never run DeepSeek's `curl -k -u`; validate TLS and protect all secrets from process lists/logs
Do not clear SEL/syslog; retain chronology and verify no time change
Stop on unexpected writable operation, time jump, authentication downgrade or target expansion outside the approved subtree
Restore temporary SNMPv3 account/settings only through the approved UI path; no automatic retry
expected_evidence: BMC model/firmware plus vendor MIB name/version/hash and `$target` numeric expansion
Redacted WebUI SNMPv3 configuration and client/security profile
Full numeric and symbolic traversal with ASN.1 type/access/value decoding
Reference timestamps, timezone interpretation, delta calculation and optional separately labeled Redfish cross-check
Before/after BMC time and log chronology plus configuration cleanup
test_case.recovery: No clock mutation is part of this case. On authentication, target-expansion or time discrepancy, stop, preserve the query/MIB/reference evidence, disable only the temporary approved SNMPv3 configuration, and escalate. If any unintended time change is observed, preserve logs and use the project time-recovery procedure before further testing.

source_conflict.preserved_original_conflict: The item contains `configureSP`, while all source operations are reads and DeepSeek introduces Redfish.
source_conflict.resolution: Treat the complete item as a MIB target label and follow the explicit Get-only procedure/criteria; reject both inferred SET and Redfish substitution.

blocked.reason: Core semantics are fixed by the source's explicit retrieval verbs. MIB/OID/format/tolerance are Project Configuration prerequisites.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Platform MIB/hash, target expansion, required OIDs/types, timezone/format/tolerance and secure SNMPv3 profile.
